# Dhammasaṅgaṇī-mūlaṭīkā (Tika Abh01t)

**ID:** Tika Abh01t  
**Section:** Tīkā Dhammasaṅgaṇī-mūlaṭīkā (tika-abh01)  
**Collection:** Tika-Abhidhamma  
**Title (Pali):** Dhammasaṅgaṇī-mūlaṭīkā  
**tipitaka.org (CST):** [https://tipitaka.org/romn/](https://tipitaka.org/romn/)

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Dhammasaṅgaṇī-mūlaṭīkā* is a Pali sub-commentary (*mūlaṭīkā*) on the first book of the Abhidhammapiṭaka, the *Dhammasaṅgaṇī* (specifically commenting upon its commentary, the *Atthasālinī*) [Gal 2003; Ronkin 2005]. Bibliographical records also identify it under the alternative designations *Atthasālinī-mūlaṭīkā* and *Paramatthapakāsanī I* [Nyanatusita 2008]. In modern philosophical scholarship, the text is cited for its scholastic elucidations of Abhidhamma metaphysics and psychological theory; Maria Heim notes its analysis of intention (*cetanā*), where the sub-commentary defines the nature of intention (*cetanābhāva*) as "work" (*byāpāra*), characterizes its extensive duty, and compares its relation to accompanying mental factors to carefulness or respect (*ādara*) [Heim 2014]. The text has been accessed and cited via the Burmese-script Chaṭṭhasaṅgāyana edition [Nyanaponika and Bodhi 2012; Heim 2014].

**Sources**

- [Heim 2014] Maria Heim, Forerunner of All Things: Buddhaghosa on Mind, Intention, and Agency (2014) — Explication of intention (cetanā) as byāpāra and ādara citing the Myanmar edition
- [Nyanatusita 2008] Bhikkhu Nyanatusita, Reference Table of Pali Literature (2008) — Alternative titles Atthasālinī-mūlaṭīkā and Paramatthapakāsanī I
- [Nyanaponika and Bodhi 2012] Nyanaponika Thera and Bhikkhu Bodhi, Abhidhamma Studies: Buddhist Explorations of Consciousness and Time (2012) — Abbreviation DhsMt and reference to Burmese Chatthasangāyana edition
- [Gal 2003] Noa Gal, Metaphysics of Experience: From the Buddha’s Teaching to the Abhidhamma (2003) — Identification as Dhammasaṅgaṇī sub-commentary
- [Ronkin 2005] Noa Ronkin, Early Buddhist Metaphysics (2005) — Identification as Dhammasaṅgaṇī sub-commentary
